title: 智能車房內部空間自主重組極限 34/90 AUTONOMOUS INTERIOR RECONFIGURATION OF INTELLIGENT MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT AUTONOMOUS INTERIOR RECONFIGURATION OF INTELLIGENT MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition in the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 34 of 90). It examines whether the same bounded, physically empty mobile-habitat research chamber can be reconfigured into bedroom, workspace and common-room modes using instrumented movable furniture without losing evidence about moving-object collisions, load transfer, service continuity or physical stopping. Its core coupling is Spatial Sensing x Robotic Furniture x Autonomous Configuration. Proposed tests use scaled, unoccupied furniture, instrumented partitions, dummy anthropometric fixtures and hardware-in-the-loop controls. No genuine habitation, fire qualification, live-human safety, roadworthiness or certified robotic dwelling is claimed. The source-contract candidate is intentionally falsifiable: under matched material, mass, whole-system energy, sensing, time, computation and human-assistance budgets, a frozen interior reconfiguration policy should improve measured envelope leakage without worsening deployment time. The physical research must separate this unusual envelope-services endpoint from functional floor-area gain. Strong alternatives are competent manual rearrangement, well-designed passive convertible furniture and conventional static interiors performing equivalent activities. Concealed desk stops, nonholonomic casters, a wall-bed support omission, ambiguous rail engagement, depth-camera reflections, shared sensor drift, unobserved power, utility-hose tension and blocked egress-proxy geometry can defeat the claim. Failed missions and deliberate refusals remain in the complete denominator. Thirty distinct mathematical plates cover configuration-space collision sets, swept-volume clearance, contact and engagement truth, sequence timing and deadlock, trajectory dynamics, actuator torque and braking, support-polygon stability, safe-set and hard-stop conditions, electrical and thermal work, moving-utility water mass balance, airflow, load-path reserve, sensor covariance, complete-denominator outcomes and statistical tail risk. The source F34 formula, Delta S_w = Q_in - Q_use - Q_loss - Q_out for integrated volumes over a specified interval, is retained as a conditional moving-water-services balance, not presented as the governing law of indoor autonomous furniture. Every research plate specifies model construction, native units, identifiability limits, blinded disproof and chapter links. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated investigations of convertible room tasks, shared motion paths, occluded surfaces, rolling-base kinematics, hidden furniture contact, electrical and wet services, safe human-like clearance proxies, constrained comparison, independent calibration, authority to stop and long-cycle material wear. Two hundred individually worded Research Gates require experiment-specific physical witnesses, concealed interventions, competing explanations and disqualifying thresholds. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose distinguishable instruments and evidence devices: for example a rail-engagement microscope, a bed support cradle, a hose-bend witness, a pinch-force sensor, an occlusion testing rig and an unselected-mission register. These remain proposed prototypes; no fabricated system is represented as a tested breakthrough. Scientific limitations are integral to this edition. Geometry alone does not establish real functional use; controller agreement does not guarantee independent physical truth; a positive sensor score cannot override missing support, uncertain utilities or a failed stop. The methodological literature includes Xiong et al. on convertible indoor scene motion planning (DOI 10.1109/TVCG.2020.3005680), Xiong et al. on coordinated reconfigurable furniture (DOI 10.1002/cav.70113), Hauser et al. on Roombots furniture research (DOI 10.1016/j.robot.2020.103467), Tang et al. on dense mobile-furniture coordination (DOI 10.1109/LRA.2025.3577423), and Dudek et al. on shape-morphing metamaterials (DOI 10.1038/s41578-025-00828-9). These are relevant antecedents, not tests of the integrated F34 hypothesis. Author-supplied mother-lineage DOI identifiers 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 are retained without independent metadata confirmation. The manuscript is an internally QA-checked, hypothesis-generating working edition, not a completed experimental study or externally peer-reviewed scientific validation.
